<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown check --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown check [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

## Arguments

`<PATH>`
: The drive or folder to check. It must be there now (connected and mounted).

## Options

`--list`
: List every file that has no copy elsewhere.

`--json`
: Print it as JSON, for scripts.

`--jobs <JOBS>`
: Readers per device; 1 suits spinning disks, raise it for SSDs. Default: `1`.

`--retry-errors`
: Retry files that failed to read last time.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

Exits 0 when every file has a SHA-256-identical copy outside PATH ("SAFE TO WIPE"), and 2 when some files exist nowhere else or couldn't be read ("COPY FIRST"). Copies on drives that aren't connected still count: the verdict is about the index. `--list` lists the largest 20,000 such files. Empty files don't count against a drive.

## Examples

```sh
backdown check /media/old-drive
# every file that has no copy, largest first
backdown check /media/old-drive --list
# in a script: 0 = safe to wipe, 2 = copy first
backdown check /media/old-drive && echo "safe to wipe"
```
